text:
incident-bot: PAGER triggered: AUTH-PROXY_HIGH_4xx — sudden spike of 4xx (mostly 401) to auth-proxy from 3 external IPs. Affected services: hosted-auth, token-introspection. Pager: @sre-oncall @security-lead — please triage. Thread 3250001111

alice.m: seeing alert in Datadog. spike began ~10:03 UTC. sample traces show many `POST /v1/auth/token` with different bearer tokens in Authorization header.

sre-oncall: I'm on it. pulling auth-proxy logs + pcap from ingress. @bob.t can you pull s3 bucket prod-auth-logs for 10:00-10:10 and grep for `POST /v1/auth/token`?

bob.t: grabbing slices now. note: user-agent across hits is `curl/7.68.0` and X-Forwarded-For looks forged. quick grep snippet: ```grep "POST /v1/auth/token" auth.log | head -n 20``` — I'll upload filtered output to secure bucket.

charlie.g: any 5xx or latency impact for downstream services/customers?

alice.m: no 5xx, downstream is healthy. but we have ~0.4% of customer auths failing during window — some sessions rejected.

security-lead: initial read: looks like credential stuffing or token replay. assume tokens may be leaked. short-term actions: block those 3 IPs at edge, enable WAF rule to drop suspicious UA/header combos, rotate any service keys that might be in debug logs. long-term: audit logger behavior and scrub any leaked secrets. @sre-oncall do blocks now.

sre-oncall: blocking IPs now: `iptables -A INPUT -s 1.2.3.4 -j DROP` (applied), then 5.6.7.8 and 9.10.11.12. traffic dropped to baseline after second block. monitoring.

alice.m: uploaded filtered log slice to s3://sec-incident-3250001111/log-slices/ ; bucket ACLs set to org-security only. FYI I found token-like strings in debug logs emitted by staging-forwarder service — looks like debug logger forwarded Authorization header to prod logs earlier. example pattern: `tok_abc123...`

security-lead: if debug logs contained Authorization headers, we must assume exposed tokens. immediate: rotate service creds for any principals that could have leaked, revoke sessions if necessary. who owns the staging-forwarder / telemetry pipeline?

bob.t: telemetry/forwarder owned by infra-team; affected principal: svc-telemetry-42. exposed tokens include both ephemeral session tokens and one long-lived telemetry token.

charlie.g: proposed plan: 1) revoke svc-telemetry-42 keys 2) deploy new key 3) patch logger to strip Authorization header and re-deploy 4) scrub S3 for token patterns. who will execute?

alice.m: infra will handle deploys. I'm starting a key rotate for svc-telemetry-42 now and patching logger env to drop Authorization in logs. patch snippet: ```kubectl set env deployment/telemetry-forwarder AUTH_TOKEN=<new> -n infra; kubectl rollout restart deploy/telemetry-forwarder -n infra```

security-lead: legal/PR standby: prepare for potential customer notice if we confirm tokens tied to customer accounts. collect evidence (MD5, export paths).

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged. Escalation level set to P1. Incident commander: security-lead.

sre-oncall: rotated keys for svc-telemetry-42, deployments updated and rolled. started scrub job to remove token patterns from prod-auth-logs: `python tools/scrub_logs.py --bucket prod-auth-logs --prefix 2026-03-16/ --pattern 'tok_' --secure-delete` — running under org-security creds. ETA ~3m.

alice.m: scrub job started — logging job ID 0x7f2. also added canary WAF rule to block requests with header `"X-Debug: true"`.

security-lead: good. forensic note: suspicious S3 GETs from the external IPs and one AWS principal arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/unknown-accessor at ~10:06 UTC. bob, can you pull CloudTrail for the bucket?

bob.t: pulled CloudTrail and exported to s3://sec-incident-3250001111/cloudtrail.json.gz (permissioned to sec-only). found GET object events from IPs 1.2.3.4/5/6 and that IAM role. raising IAM review ticket to rotate credentials for that role and suspend sessions.

charlie.g: IAM recommendation: disable role keys pending investigation. @security-lead ok to rotate all roles that had read access to prod-auth-logs?

security-lead: approve. rotate, revoke, capture artifacts. ensure CloudTrail export preserved for legal.

alice.m: uploaded checksums and evidence: md5: e3b0c44298fc1c... to the secure folder.

sre-oncall: monitoring metrics show no repeat anomalous token use after blocks + rotations. I'll hold monitoring and hand off to night oncall in ~6h. please include rotated keys list and evidence paths in handoff.

security-lead: for the handoff: include - list of rotated principals (svc-telemetry-42, role/unknown-accessor rotated/disabled) - S3 evidence path s3://sec-incident-3250001111/ - CloudTrail export path - scrub job ID and its log - outstanding tasks: full log sweep across all buckets, verify no other services forwarded Authorization headers, coordinate customer comms if PII confirmed.

alice.m: created incident draft: https://internal.redwood/ops/incidents/3250001111 (draft) with the above.

bob.t: will prepare a short post-incident checklist and coordinate with legal for cust-comms if required.

sre-oncall: lowering pager to monitor-only. status: mitigated (blocks applied, keys rotated, scrub job running). :white_check_mark:

security-lead: incident commander handing to oncall-night. If telemetry spikes or token usage resumes, re-open P1. Thanks team. :heart:

(reacts: alice.m :thumbsup:, bob.t :eyes:, sre-oncall :white_check_mark:)
